caseTitle: Bilateral Hip Dysplasia & Successful Stem-Cell PRP Therapy
condition: Severe lameness in hind legs, difficulty rising, graded Stage 3 osteoarthritis.
diagnosis: Canine Hip Dysplasia confirmed via orthogonal radiographic imaging showing 45% joint laxity.
treatment: Ultrasound-guided Platelet-Rich Plasma (PRP) autologous injection combined with 6-week underwater treadmill hydrotherapy and low-impact laser sessions.
outcome: 95% restoration of pain-free range of motion. Patient running without NSAID dependency after 8 weeks.

caseTitle: Emergency Management of Feline Lower Urinary Tract Disease (FLUTD)
condition: Acute stranguria, hematuria, vocal distress, and partial urethral obstruction.
diagnosis: Struvite crystal urolithiasis with inflammatory urethral spasm identified by abdominal ultrasound and urinalysis (pH 7.8).
treatment: Emergency sterile retrograde urethral hydropropulsion, 48-hr indwelling urinary catheter, urinary acidifier dietary transition (c/d Multicare), and buprenorphine analgesia.
outcome: Obstruction fully relieved. Urinalysis normalized to pH 6.4 within 14 days without surgical perineal urethrostomy.

condition: Tail bobbing, open-mouth dyspnea, lethargy, and loss of vocalization.
diagnosis: Fungal granuloma in caudal thoracic air sac visualized through micro-endoscopy.
treatment: Daily closed-chamber Voriconazole micro-nebulization therapy coupled with systemic antifungal amphotericin B and vitamin A nutritional supplementation.
outcome: Granuloma completely resolved on follow-up radiography. Full vocal agility and flying endurance restored.

caseTitle: Minimally Invasive Soft Palate Coblation for BOAS
condition: Severe inspiratory stridor, exercise intolerance, and nocturnal obstructive sleep apnea.
diagnosis: Brachycephalic Obstructive Airway Syndrome (Elongated soft palate & stenotic nares).
treatment: Radiofrequency coblation staphylectomy (shortening soft palate) and laser alar fold resection under total intravenous anesthesia.
outcome: Airway resistance reduced by 78%. Snoring eliminated; patient successfully participated in standard 30-minute outdoor walks in summer temperatures.
